new_entities.name: Chronic heat exposure in men
new_entities.description: Repeated occupational, environmental, or recreational heat exposure in men over weeks or months.

new_entities.name: Sperm concentration
new_entities.description: The concentration of spermatozoa in semen, usually expressed as millions per milliliter.

edges.effect_quant: The clearest pooled estimate comes from the 2022 meta-analysis, where high ambient temperature exposure was associated with substantially lower sperm concentration (SMD -1.07, 95% CI -1.42 to -0.72). A 2024 multi-center analysis of 33,234 men also found hot-season heat anomalies negatively associated with sperm concentration, and the classic sauna-intervention study showed marked but reversible suppression of spermatogenesis after repeated sauna exposure.
edges.population: men exposed chronically to high ambient, occupational, or recreational heat while of reproductive age
edges.mechanism: Spermatogenesis depends on the testes staying cooler than core body temperature. Repeated heat exposure can disrupt Sertoli-cell support, mitochondrial function, chromatin packaging, and germ-cell survival, which makes reduced sperm concentration biologically plausible rather than merely correlational.
edges.summary: This is a real and fairly intuitive male-fertility harm edge. The literature is not perfect on exposure definition, but across meta-analytic, cohort, and intervention-style data, chronic heat exposure consistently pushes sperm concentration in the wrong direction.
edges.caveats: The magnitude varies by source and timing of heat exposure, acclimatization, and whether the exposure is occupational, environmental, or voluntary sauna use. Some heat-related impairments are reversible, so this should be read as a modifiable harm signal rather than permanent infertility.

evidence.citation: Durairajanayagam D et al 2022 Iran J Public Health
evidence.notes: The Impact of High Ambient Temperature on Human Sperm Parameters: A Meta-Analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: high ambient temperature exposure versus non-exposure for sperm concentration

evidence.notes: Effects of temperature anomaly on sperm quality: A multi-center study of 33,234 men.

evidence.citation: Garolla A et al 2013 Hum Reprod
evidence.notes: Seminal and molecular evidence that sauna exposure affects human spermatogenesis.
